next_steps.text: CMS suggests comparing your bill with your EOB, both the services and the amount you owe, and paying only after you’ve checked that they match.

sources.title: How to read your medical bill

next_steps.text: CMS suggests asking the provider’s billing department for a list of the costs for each item or service you’re being billed for.

sources.title: Check your medical bill for errors

next_steps.text: For questions about a bill, or an error on your bill or EOB, CMS says to contact your provider or facility.

sources.title: How to read your medical bill

next_steps.text: CMS says an Explanation of Benefits (EOB) isn’t a bill. It shows how much your plan covers and what you’ll pay when you get a bill from your provider.

sources.title: How to read a health insurance explanation of benefits

comparison.disclaimer: These are differences worth asking about, not findings that anything is wrong. A bill and an EOB can differ for ordinary reasons, such as a payment you already made or a service on a separate EOB. PatientShield doesn't decide whether a bill is correct; your provider and your plan can explain each line.
